questions.question: Read the following passage and answer the given questions accordingly: The concept of 'Deep Time' challenges the human tendency to view history through the lens of anthropocentrism. Geologically, human existence is but a flickering candle in the vast darkness of Earth's 4.5 billion-year history. This perspective is not merely a scientific curiosity; it is a moral imperative. By understanding the immense spans of time that preceded us and will follow us, we might cultivate a sense of 'intergenerational justice'—a responsibility to the future that transcends our immediate, short-term desires. However, our cognitive architecture is ill-equipped for this. We are evolved to respond to immediate threats and rewards, a trait often referred to as 'temporal myopia.' Overcoming this myopia requires a radical shift in how we value the 'unborn'—those billions of humans and non-humans who will inherit a world shaped by our current ecological and technological choices. Q- According to the passage, why is 'Deep Time' considered a moral imperative?
